scope: Baltor development on this workstation; references only, no credential values

kaggle-research-primary.note: Owner-authorized Kaggle access from the existing local token file, stored in the system keyring. Only bounded metadata and rights-reviewed public-source reads are selected. No competition joining, rule acceptance, upload, notebook execution or dataset bulk download is implied.

huggingface-research-primary.note: Owner-supplied Hub token. This installation permits metadata reads only, regardless of broader token permissions. No publishing, gated-data download or model execution is implied.

serper-search-primary.note: Owner-supplied Serper credential. Initial validation and later collection require explicit request and spend ceilings; provider-account limits remain shared across key aliases.

jina-research-primary.note: Owner-supplied Jina credential. Reader, search, embedding and rerank are distinct operations; qualify and budget each before activation. No unbounded crawl or batch inference is authorized by this reference.

openalex-research-primary.note: Owner-supplied OpenAlex credential. Use authorization headers, retain source-level quotas and holds, and verify reported limits before increasing the selected collection ceiling.

brave-search-primary.note: Owner-supplied search credential. Initial validation is bounded and ephemeral; storage rights and shared account limits must be established before persistent collection. No purchase or quota circumvention is authorized.

exa-search-primary.note: Owner-supplied Exa credential. Follow the build-with-exa skill for request semantics. Initial validation uses search only, without creating monitors, agent runs or another recurring schedule.

tavily-search-primary.note: Owner-supplied Tavily credential. Initial validation is bounded; source, cost and account limits remain separate from having a usable key. No automatic purchase or unbounded crawl.

ollama-cloud-search.note: Existing owner-supplied environment credential, persisted in the system keyring for the bounded research timer. The named executor retains its 300-request daily ceiling; this reference authorizes no purchase or additional model allowance.

cloudflare-r2-management.note: The owner supplied an account-wide R2 admin token on October 6, 2026 and requested persistent keyring storage. This reference grants no new effect authority: operations remain confined to explicitly selected Baltor resources; resource deletion still requires the owner's instruction.

cloudflare-r2-sample-access-id.note: S3 access-key identifier supplied by the owner on October 6, 2026. The issued token has account-wide R2 admin scope; the canary is confined to the existing private baltor-catalogue-bodies-sample bucket. The reference name describes its initial use, not a provider-enforced bucket restriction.

cloudflare-r2-sample-secret.note: S3 secret supplied by the owner on October 6, 2026, stored only in the system keyring. Paired with cloudflare-r2-sample-access-id. The issued token is account-wide R2 admin; code limits the canary to the named Baltor bucket. Production selection remains a separate verified operation.

stripe-live.note: The live account, separate from the sandbox. The owner chose a full secret key on 2026-09-21 and instructed that it be kept; the slot therefore accepts one. A restricted key is also accepted. Test keys are refused, so a live operation cannot silently run against practice data and the reverse cannot happen either.

stripe-live-webhook-secret.note: The signing secret of the live subscription webhook endpoint we_1UI5ZI2IF9bCskLc19SrJ4lq. The provider shows it once, at creation. The service uses it to prove an event really came from the provider.

tactical-model-generation.note: The owner's Tactical Engineering model server, which also answers as iamretarded.net. The owner supplied the key on 2026-09-23. The candidate generator and the review panel's provider_binding reviewer resolve it only inside the process that makes the call, through the committed provider binding.
